exam_guide_revision: Practical Python data-stack curriculum reviewed against current official NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, and Seaborn documentation on 2026-09-19.

domain.name: NumPy: Arrays, Shapes, Axes & Vectorized Computation

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; retrieval questions and typed coding questions provide the scored signal.

authoring_notes: Interactive first-pass learning for NumPy. Prompts use exact cloze versions of their revealed text and progress from purpose/mental models to code patterns and gotchas.

modules.title: Choose and use common array-analysis functions

nodes.title: Choose an operation from the goal

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Start with the __________, then choose the NumPy operation that performs that transformation.

reveal.text: Start with the analysis goal, then choose the NumPy operation that performs that transformation.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: `reshape` changes __________, `where` chooses conditionally, `unique` finds distinct values, and `argsort` returns sorting indices.

reveal.text: `reshape` changes shape, `where` chooses conditionally, `unique` finds distinct values, and `argsort` returns sorting indices.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: `sort` returns sorted __________; `argsort` returns the indices that would produce that order.

reveal.text: `sort` returns sorted values; `argsort` returns the indices that would produce that order.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `np.where(condition, a, b)` chooses values from `a` where the condition is __________ and from `b` otherwise.

reveal.text: `np.where(condition, a, b)` chooses values from `a` where the condition is true and from `b` otherwise.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use `where` when the output should be chosen __________ for every element from a condition.

reveal.text: Use `where` when the output should be chosen elementwise for every element from a condition.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Replace negatives with zero using `clean = np.where(x < 0, __________, x)`.

reveal.text: Replace negatives with zero using `clean = np.where(x < 0, 0, x)`.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `np.unique` finds distinct values; `np.argsort` returns __________ rather than sorted values.

reveal.text: `np.unique` finds distinct values; `np.argsort` returns sorting indices rather than sorted values.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Get distinct labels and counts with `np.unique(labels, __________=True)`.

reveal.text: Get distinct labels and counts with `np.unique(labels, return_counts=True)`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Use `np.sort(x)` when you need sorted values; use `np.argsort(x)` when you need to reorder __________ arrays consistently.

reveal.text: Use `np.sort(x)` when you need sorted values; use `np.argsort(x)` when you need to reorder related arrays consistently.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: For a reduction, `axis` identifies the dimension being __________.

reveal.text: For a reduction, `axis` identifies the dimension being collapsed.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: For shape `(rows, columns)`, `axis=0` collapses __________ and leaves one result per column.

reveal.text: For shape `(rows, columns)`, `axis=0` collapses rows and leaves one result per column.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: `axis=-1` means the __________ dimension, which is often the feature/column dimension in a 2-D array.

reveal.text: `axis=-1` means the last dimension, which is often the feature/column dimension in a 2-D array.

nodes.title: Mean, sum, std, min, and max

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Reduction functions summarize many values into __________ values along a chosen axis.

reveal.text: Reduction functions summarize many values into fewer values along a chosen axis.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Use `mean` for an average, `sum` for a total, and `std` for __________.

reveal.text: Use `mean` for an average, `sum` for a total, and `std` for spread.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: For `x.shape == (100, 4)`, one mean per feature is `np.mean(x, axis=__________)`.

reveal.text: For `x.shape == (100, 4)`, one mean per feature is `np.mean(x, axis=0)`.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `keepdims=True` keeps each reduced axis with size __________ instead of removing it.

reveal.text: `keepdims=True` keeps each reduced axis with size 1 instead of removing it.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Keep the reduced dimension when the result should broadcast naturally back across the original __________.

reveal.text: Keep the reduced dimension when the result should broadcast naturally back across the original array.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: For `x.shape == (100, 3)`, `x.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)` has shape __________.

reveal.text: For `x.shape == (100, 3)`, `x.mean(axis=0, keepdims=True)` has shape `(1, 3)`.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `reshape` changes an array's dimensions while preserving the total number of __________.

reveal.text: `reshape` changes an array's dimensions while preserving the total number of elements.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: A flat 12-element array can become 3×4 with `x.reshape(__________, 4)`.

reveal.text: A flat 12-element array can become 3×4 with `x.reshape(3, 4)`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: A requested shape is invalid if its dimension sizes multiply to a different __________ count.

reveal.text: A requested shape is invalid if its dimension sizes multiply to a different element count.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: `concatenate` joins along an __________ axis; `stack` creates a new axis.

reveal.text: `concatenate` joins along an existing axis; `stack` creates a new axis.

prompts.label: 🧠 MENTAL MODEL
prompts.placeholder: Two `(3,4)` arrays stacked on axis 0 become `(__________,3,4)`.

reveal.text: Two `(3,4)` arrays stacked on axis 0 become `(2,3,4)`.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: Concatenating those same arrays on axis 0 produces `(6,4)`, so it does __________ increase `ndim`.

reveal.text: Concatenating those same arrays on axis 0 produces `(6,4)`, so it does not increase `ndim`.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: Broadcasting lets compatible shapes participate in elementwise operations without explicitly __________ the smaller array.

reveal.text: Broadcasting lets compatible shapes participate in elementwise operations without explicitly repeating the smaller array.

prompts.label: 🎯 WHEN?
prompts.placeholder: Column statistics with shape `(features,)` can broadcast across data with shape `(rows, __________)`.

reveal.text: Column statistics with shape `(features,)` can broadcast across data with shape `(rows, features)`.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: Vectorized column standardization follows `(x - x.mean(axis=0)) / __________`.

reveal.text: Vectorized column standardization follows `(x - x.mean(axis=0)) / x.std(axis=0)`.
